provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: My growth chart
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what helps them grow.
The pupils should be able to identify their height on a chart.
Introduction:
We all grow bigger like our plants in the school garden.
Today we will learn how we grow.
Content:
Growth means getting taller and stronger.
Good food like rice and beans helps us grow.
Sleep helps our body rest and grow.
We can measure our height on a growth chart.
Class activity:
Let's line up and measure each child's height.
We will mark the height on our class chart.
Evaluation questions:
What helps us grow?
How do we measure our height?
What happens when we sleep?
Summary:
Good food and sleep help us grow tall and strong.

topics.title: Balanced plate
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list foods that make them glow.
The pupils should be able to arrange a balanced plate.
Introduction:
Yesterday we learned about growth.
Today we learn about the foods that help us grow.
Content:
A balanced plate has different foods.
Half our plate should have fruits and vegetables.
Go foods like yam give us energy.
Grow foods like beans make us strong.
Glow foods like carrots make our skin nice.
Class activity:
We will make a paper plate with different foods.
Each child will place food pictures on their plate.
Evaluation questions:
What should be half of our plate?
Name a go food.
What do glow foods do for us?
Summary:
A balanced plate helps us grow strong and healthy.

topics.title: Care of the eyes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state rules for eye care.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate resting the eyes.
Introduction:
Our eyes help us see the world.
We must take good care of our eyes.
Content:
We should not read in the dark.
Reading in dark hurts our eyes.
After watching TV or phone, we rest our eyes.
We can close our eyes for a minute.
If something hurts our eyes, tell mummy.
Class activity:
We will play a game of closing our eyes for 30 seconds.
Then we will draw what we saw with open eyes.
Evaluation questions:
What should we not do in the dark?
How do we rest our eyes?
Who should we tell if our eyes hurt?
Summary:
We must protect our eyes to see well.

topics.title: Care of the teeth
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list foods that harm teeth.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate proper brushing.
Introduction:
Our teeth help us eat our food.
We must keep our teeth clean and strong.
Content:
Too many sweets hurt our teeth.
Sweets make tiny holes in our teeth.
We should brush our teeth every morning.\Brushing keeps teeth white and strong.
We visit the dentist with mummy.
Class activity:
We will practice brushing with our toothbrushes.
Each child will brush a model teeth.
Evaluation questions:
What foods hurt our teeth?
How often should we brush?
Who helps us when our teeth hurt?
Summary:
Clean teeth help us eat and smile well.

topics.title: Road safety basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state crossing rules.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate safe walking.
Introduction:
We walk to school every day.
We must know how to cross roads safely.
Content:
We always stop at the road edge.
We look left and right for cars.
We cross only with an adult.
We walk on the inside of the road.
We do not run on the road.
Class activity:
We will practice stopping and looking before crossing.
We will walk in a line like we are crossing the road.
Evaluation questions:
What do we do before crossing the road?
Who should we cross with?
Where do we walk on the road?
Summary:
Road safety keeps us safe from accidents.

topics.title: Sharp objects are dangerous
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify sharp objects.
The pupils should be able to state what to do with sharp objects.
Introduction:
Some objects can hurt us.
We must be careful with sharp things.
Content:
Knives, blades and scissors are sharp.
Sharp objects can cut our skin.
We should not play with sharp objects.
If we see a sharp object, we tell an adult.
Adults keep sharp objects away from children.
Class activity:
We will sort objects into sharp and not sharp.
We will practice saying 'sharp' for dangerous objects.
Evaluation questions:
Name a sharp object.
What should we not do with sharp objects?
Who should we tell if we see a sharp object?
Summary:
Sharp objects are dangerous and we must be careful.

topics.title: Fire and hot things
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify hot objects.
The pupils should be able to state fire safety rules.
Introduction:
Fire is hot but useful.
We must be careful with fire and hot things.
Content:
Pots on the stove are very hot.
Fire can burn our skin badly.
We should not touch pots or fire.
If we see smoke, we shout for help.
We run away from fire and tell mummy.
Class activity:
We will point to pictures of hot objects.
We will practice shouting 'fire' and running to the teacher.
Evaluation questions:
What should we not touch?
What do we do when we see smoke?
Who should we tell about fire?
Summary:
Fire is dangerous and we must stay away from it.

topics.title: Mosquito and malaria
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state how mosquitoes bite.
The pupils should be able to list ways to prevent malaria.
Introduction:
Mosquitoes are small insects.
They can make us sick with malaria.
Content:
Mosquitoes bite us at night.
Their bite makes us have malaria.
We sleep under treated nets.
We clear stagnant water where mosquitoes live.
Mummy takes us to the clinic when we are sick.
Class activity:
We will pretend to sleep under a net.
We will act like mosquitoes buzzing around.
Evaluation questions:
What do mosquito bites cause?
How do we protect ourselves at night?
Where do mosquitoes lay their eggs?
Summary:
We must protect ourselves from mosquito bites.

topics.title: Clean environment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state why clean environment is important.
The pupils should be able to identify things that make environment dirty.
Introduction:
Our school is clean and nice.
A dirty place can make us sick.
Content:
We sweep our classroom every day.
We pick litter and put it in the bin.
Bushes and gutters have stagnant water.
Stagnant water breeds mosquitoes.
Mosquitoes give us malaria.
Class activity:
We will sweep a small area with small brooms.
We will collect litter and put it in the bin.
Evaluation questions:
What should we do to keep our environment clean?
Where do mosquitoes breed?
Why is a clean environment important?
Summary:
A clean environment keeps us healthy.

topics.title: Revision and health quiz
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to answer health questions.
The pupils should be able to make a healthy plate.
Introduction:
We have learned many health habits.
Today we will play a quiz game.
Content:
We will answer questions about what we learned.
We will make a paper plate with healthy foods.
The teacher will ask questions about health habits.
We will clap for correct answers.
Class activity:
We will play a quiz game with health questions.
Each child will make a healthy plate with food pictures.
Evaluation questions:
What helps us grow?
How do we cross the road safely?
What do we do to protect our eyes?
Summary:
We remember all the health habits to stay healthy.
